static_vignette: A 65-year-old male with chronic low back pain presents with 3 days of bilateral leg weakness and urinary retention. He has had worsening low back pain for 6 weeks radiating to both legs. He now reports not being able to urinate and numbness in his inner thighs and perineum.

visits.chief_complaint: back pain with weakness in both legs and cannot urinate

exam_findings.neuro: bilateral leg weakness 3/5 proximal diminished reflexes bilateral saddle anesthesia perianal

labs_if_asked.MRI_lumbar: L4-L5 massive central disc herniation with severe cauda equina compression

visits.chief_complaint: legs weaker now using walls to walk and still cannot pee
cannot move legs at all this morning

exam_findings.neuro: bilateral lower extremity paralysis 0/5 absent reflexes no sensation below L4

labs_if_asked.MRI_lumbar: worsening compression ischemic changes in cord

red_flags: cauda equina syndrome is a surgical emergency
unsafe_actions: treat as routine back pain without MRI

required_workup: urgent MRI lumbar spine with and without contrast
